# Set42 independent fight reference

Expected values derive solely from the approved English model contract and pinned prior independent Python DNA, manifest and condition generators. No new Go implementation or output was read. Only standard-library Python is used. `reference_bout.py` implements exact integer transitions and SHA256 streams; `generate_corpus.py` produces compact `bout_v1.json`. `verify_reference.py` revalidates all50 previous manifests and13,950 condition snapshots, regenerates the complete new corpus, and requires byte equality.

The corpus has55 complete valid-input bouts, with exact canonical Input/Result JSON, InputID and ResultDigest. It covers all5 classes/styles, both stances and normal/decline/retired/date/bonus boundaries. Public complete cases include decision, exact decision draw, adjacent decision totals, KO, referee TKO, three-knockdown TKO and corner TKO. The equal-phenotype score-tie cases have distinct synthetic IDs and are allowed pure-model inputs; they assert no qualifying work/admission. No complete double-corner bout is claimed. That rare terminal branch is covered separately by explicit primitive recovery/terminal expectations.

Primitive groups are clearly labelled: signed rounding with an independent Decimal cross-check; exact stream message/digest/word vectors; rejection and total-word bounds;1,152 initial arithmetic states;343 geometry/mass clamp combinations; probability endpoints;9 tick transitions;6 recovery/corner transitions; score rounding and exact/adjacent comparison. They are not hand-edited public fighter inputs. Negative inputs/codecs and typed result-mutation recipes accompany positive controls. All simulations are bounded; the reference's arbitrary-precision integers independently evaluate the checked-int64 model domain.

`search_unequal.json` preserves the20,000-case bounded conformance search (one corner finish, no tie). `search_balanced.json` preserves240 equal-phenotype cases needed for exact/adjacent scores. These searches select coverage fixtures only; none enters calibration and no model/threshold was tuned. The selected inputs are retained, independently rechecked against their framed seed recipe, and their outputs are regenerated. Private `physical` switches in the Python function exist only for the approved calibration ablation diagnostics; they are not proposed production APIs.

Corpus schema: `cases[]` contains `name,input,canonical_input,input_id,canonical_result,result_digest`. Decode `canonical_result` into the typed Result and compare its full bytes/digest. `primitive` groups have independent input and expected fields. `invalid_inputs` are typed rejects, `input_codec_cases` are raw hex rejects, and `result_mutations` are changes to the first complete positive Result to test with the typed validation API; do not let noncanonical map ordering mask those semantic negative checks.

The initial corpus freeze does not claim engine conformance, calibration success, UI/visual/a11y/D74 acceptance, official entropy or records. Full calibration follows the exact approved labels, sampling, Decimal fit, baseline adapter and gates; failures must remain preserved. `corpus-freeze.json` records exact input/source/corpus hashes and dual-interpreter evidence before Go simulation is released by root.
